clock_assembly_drone.subject: A compact hovering workshop drone with a round brass body, four articulated tool arms, and one bright arc-blue lens. It is assembling a single tiny Gear Wisp beneath itself: three loose cogs and a blue spark just beginning to form a simple face-like core. The drone is practical, balanced, and about the size of a large toolbox.
clock_assembly_drone.perspective: Eye-level three-quarter view with the drone centered and the nascent Gear Wisp directly beneath it as a clearly subordinate effect; generous margin around both.
clock_assembly_drone.background: A shadowed assembly alcove of cool iron shelving and blurred hanging chains, punctuated by restrained amber task lights that separate the polished brass body.
clock_assembly_drone.notes: Keep the drone as the one primary subject. The summoned Gear Wisp is small, unfinished, and visually secondary; no swarm of helpers.

clock_bronze_frame.subject: A small, narrow humanoid construct whose body is literally a freestanding bronze armature: open rib-like struts, precise hinge joints, a round arc-blue core, and no bulky armor. It stands on a workbench and presents a freshly ejected blank parchment sheet from a slot in its chest, like a quiet mechanical herald. The design is useful and slightly worn, not heroic or intimidating.

clock_bronze_frame.background: A dark clockmaker's workshop of charcoal iron and cool blue shadow, with only a few dim amber bench lamps and softly blurred tools; strong value contrast behind the polished bronze frame.

clock_clockwork_sniper.subject: A compact humanoid Clockwright construct crouches behind a waist-high stone parapet, roughly human-sized rather than towering. Its narrow brass torso, oiled-steel joints, and single arc-blue lens are built for precision, not intimidation. One forearm unfolds into a restrained spring-driven bolt caster aligned with the glowing lens; at its tip, a small needle-thin arc-blue aiming spark marks the instant before firing. The opposite three-fingered hand braces naturally on the parapet. A few exposed gears turn at the shoulder, but the silhouette stays clean and practical.

clock_clockwork_sniper.background: A pale, cold blue-grey dawn seen through a broken workshop window, softly lit and uncluttered; the darker brass-and-steel construct reads crisply against it.
clock_clockwork_sniper.notes: No enormous rifle, cannon, muzzle explosion, target reticle, scope markings, ammunition belt, cape, or battlefield destruction. Scraped from the draft brief this card was generated from (clock_clockwork_sniper).

clock_gear_overhaul.subject: One large damaged gear of cold blued steel and oxidized turquoise copper suspended in a precise ring of ivory-ceramic repair tools as cracked teeth are removed and two fresh molten-gold teeth click into place. Below it, only the blurred shoulders of a few small constructs catch the same measured golden pulse, implying a coordinated upgrade without creating competing subjects.

clock_gear_overhaul.notes: Palette priority: oxidized turquoise and blued steel subject against dusty coral and burnt-sienna atmosphere, with molten gold as the focal accent; avoid an arc-blue glow. Show improvement through exact replacement and alignment, not destruction. No readable plans, letters, numerals, or giant blast.

clock_mass_recall.subject: A vast Clockwright recall mechanism has opened like a horizontal mechanical iris: three concentric brass rings rotate backward around a brilliant arc-blue center while copper mainsprings rewind in perfect unison. One solid humanoid construct is being recalled into the aperture, cleanly separating into large armor plates, gears, and limbs that travel backward along precise curved paths; its intact upper torso remains the readable secondary silhouette, not a crowd. A few tiny distant parts from other recalled machines arc toward the same center to imply battlefield-wide scale without becoming competing subjects. The effect is orderly and exact, like time reversing a careful assembly process—not an explosion, vortex, or portal to another place.
clock_mass_recall.perspective: Steep three-quarter view into a huge circular recall aperture, with its bright center and the recalled construct's torso inside the middle 70%.
clock_mass_recall.background: A cavernous near-black assembly hall of charcoal stone and unlit iron gantries; the brass mechanism, pale recalled parts, and arc-blue rings carry nearly all the light.
clock_mass_recall.notes: No clock numerals, writing, diagrams, or rune-like marks. Scraped from the draft brief this card was generated from (clock_mass_recall).

clock_modular_stalker.subject: A sleek quadrupedal hunting construct shaped like a low mechanical panther, built from interchangeable matte black-steel modules joined by pale brass locking rings. It prowls across a frost-white stone beam with one paw lifted; two small magenta-violet memory cores are visible inside opened flank compartments, designed to release intact if the body is destroyed. A few hairline arc-blue seams remain secondary. Its silhouette is agile and predatory but still machine-like.
clock_modular_stalker.perspective: Low side three-quarter view at beam height, showing the entire stalking body from head to tail and keeping both glowing flank cores readable in the central area.
clock_modular_stalker.background: An open ruined viaduct during pale ember-snow, with a hazy ash-pink sky, bone-white masonry, and muted mauve distance. The near-black stalker reads as a clean dark silhouette against the bright outdoor background.
clock_modular_stalker.notes: Palette priority: ash pink, bone white, and mauve environment; matte black and pale brass subject; two magenta-violet cores; arc-blue only in hairline seams. The two memory cores quietly foreshadow drawing two cards on death. No gore, no prey, no pack, and no oversized monster staging.

clock_overclocker.subject: A lean, precise humanoid construct of blackened steel and pale nickel turning the red-hot governor wheel mounted in its own open chest. Verdigris-copper fingers lock onto the wheel as thin copper-orange synchronization pulses travel through a few connected cables toward indistinct friendly constructs beyond the focal plane. A single tiny arc-blue indicator remains as a restrained Clockwright signature. Its posture is controlled and technical, not berserk.
clock_overclocker.perspective: Waist-up low three-quarter view focused on the hands, governor wheel, and single bright chest core, with the full head silhouette safely inside the middle 70%.

The team-wide buff is a controlled synchronization pulse, not an explosion. Keep all other constructs indistinct and secondary.

clock_snap_bolt.subject: A palm-sized clockwork launcher at the instant its compressed spring snaps straight, driving a single heavy bronze bolt forward inside a tight ribbon of arc-blue force. The mechanism is crisp and legible: cocked jaws, released coil, one projectile, one compact impact against a cracked iron practice plate.

clock_spring_coil.subject: A squat defensive construct built around one enormous tightly wound brass mainspring. clock_spring_coil.background: A tall, nearly black foundry corridor with cold steel walls and a warm furnace glow far behind the construct, leaving the bronze coil bright against deep shadow.

clock_temporal_rewinder.subject: A dark antique-bronze rewind dial operated by one articulated mechanical hand of black iron. As the dial turns backward, a single mid-sized construct is drawn into a controlled translucent lavender-and-pale-cyan time loop and separates cleanly into ordered armor plates, gears, and springs that travel toward a compact aperture; one blank parchment card slips from the dial housing.
clock_temporal_rewinder.perspective: Oblique close view with the rewind dial as the central focal point, the dissolving construct fully visible behind it, and the mechanical hand entering from below.
clock_temporal_rewinder.background: An almost white temporal chamber dissolved into foggy ivory, faint peach, and cool lilac planes. The dark bronze dial and hand make a graphic silhouette against the luminous high-key void rather than another dark workshop.
clock_temporal_rewinder.notes: Palette priority: luminous ivory and lilac background, dark bronze focal mechanism, translucent lavender and pale cyan magic, with no orange furnace glow. Communicate returning one minion and drawing one card. The separated pieces remain orderly and intact, not shattered; no writing or numerals on the dial or parchment.

clock_the_great_mechanism.subject: A colossal autonomous clockwork engine shaped like a walking astronomical observatory: a broad oiled-steel body wrapped in interlocking brass rings, enormous counterweighted shoulders, and a crown of slowly turning gears surrounding one brilliant arc-blue lens. Its chest is open just enough to reveal a precise blue-white mainspring core, while one massive shield-like forearm plants forward as it advances. Fresh scald marks discolor the metal of one gauntlet but the fighter is alert and controlled; a single compact cinder pulse snaps from the spear tip toward a small cracked stone training effigy at the edge of the action.
ember_scalded_striker.perspective: Low close three-quarter action view with the skirmisher's full silhouette, spear, and one clearly secondary practice target contained inside the central composition.

Bone-white fingers guide one sickly green-gold soul-thread through a narrow strip of completely blank ivory parchment; at the instant the thread snaps, the finished blank strip slips free into one waiting hand. grave_deathweaver.background: A warm amber memorial workshop with dark cedar shelves, softly blurred candle niches, and muted ember-glow, providing warm value contrast behind the cool bone and iron subject.

It scrambles out of shallow water toward the viewer, flinging one tight fan of droplets while its full compact body remains readable; the creature feels ancient, weathered, and adapted to ruined wetlands.

night_viper_fang.perspective: Close eye-level three-quarter view, complete coil and head visible with generous margin and the single fang as the focal detail.

night_viper_fang.notes: Palette priority: blush, chalk white, and peach environment; charcoal-plum snake; one silver fang and small chartreuse venom bead. Modest common-card scale, no giant serpent.

storm_gust_sprite.subject: A small nimble wind elemental, child-sized but nonhuman, formed from a charcoal storm-knot wrapped in two curling storm-silver ribbons of air. Its cyan eyes and tiny gold-white sparks punctuate a clean, playful silhouette. Both ribbon-arms snap forward in quick succession, leaving two distinct crescent gust traces that visually suggest a double strike. storm_hurricane.subject: A single immense hurricane forms as a clean double helix: two distinct storm-silver wind columns orbit one shared charcoal eye, each wrapped by its own continuous gold-white lightning trace. The paired funnels repeatedly cross without merging, creating an unmistakable two-strike rhythm from bottom to top. Thin cyan pressure rings flare where the spirals cross, while ash, roof tiles, and a few tiny ember fragments sweep upward around the outer edge to show force without cluttering the center. No person or creature inside the storm; the weather effect itself is the one subject. Keep the twin structure readable rather than a chaotic cloud explosion; no faces in the clouds, no letters, symbols, or rune-shaped lightning.
storm_hurricane.perspective: Ground-level view looking slightly upward into a centered twin-helix cyclone, with both lightning traces clearly separated inside the middle 70%.

storm_lightning_bolt.subject: One compact forked lightning bolt snaps from a small charcoal storm wisp into a waist-high broken standing stone in a ruined courtyard. The gold-white core carries a thin cyan double-trace and one tight thunder-ring at impact. Show a few bright chips and a small scorch mark, not an explosion. The lightning is the sole subject; no caster, no victim, no giant sky-filling storm, and no wide environmental destruction. Convey dangerous recoil through one faint broken afterimage curling back toward the cloud.

storm_lightning_bolt.background: Muted brown-grey ruins under a dull overcast sky, grounded and low saturation so the electric gold-white and cyan strike stays distinct.
storm_lightning_bolt.notes: Scraped from the draft brief this card was generated from (storm_lightning_bolt).

storm_spark_imp.subject: A fist-sized elemental imp made from one charcoal-black core wrapped in sharp storm-silver and cyan electrical filaments. Two tiny horn-like arcs crown its head while a matched pair of gold-white spark arms snap forward in synchronized double traces, creating a crisp two-beat gesture without forming a second creature. Its compact silhouette is mischievous and volatile rather than demonic or threatening.

storm_thunder_hoof.subject: A stocky bison-sized Tempest beast with the build of a mountain ram lowers its head and takes the first powerful stride of a short forward lunge. Its coarse charcoal-and-storm-silver coat lifts slightly with static; two forward-curving dark horns carry a faint cyan edge, and each front hoof kicks up one small gold-white spark on contact with the road. A single short lightning thread joins the hooves close to the ground—no surrounding storm. The animal is muscular and durable but recognizably mortal, not an elemental titan. Keep all four legs readable.
storm_thunder_hoof.perspective: Low but natural side three-quarter view of a bison-sized beast beginning a short forward lunge, with all four hooves and both horns inside the middle 70%.
storm_thunder_hoof.background: A muted ochre quarry road under a plain overcast sky, with dull earth and low broken stone; the storm-silver hide and small cyan-gold sparks provide restrained contrast.
storm_thunder_hoof.notes: No rider, armor, giant antlers, glowing whole body, tornado, thundercloud vortex, landscape-spanning bolt, airborne pose, or shattered terrain. Scraped from the draft brief this card was generated from (storm_thunder_hoof).

storm_wind_rider.subject: A lean humanoid air elemental rides a single curved blade of compressed wind just above the rooftops, crouched like a skirmisher banking into a fast close-range sweep. Its body is charcoal cloud wrapped in storm-silver streamers, with cyan eyes and sparse gold-white sparks along the wind blade. The rider and its wind arc read as one unified silhouette, not a rider plus mount. Keep the motion local and agile: one short double-trace, a few roof tiles rattling, no tornado, no weapon, no army, and no citywide storm.
storm_wind_rider.perspective: Low dynamic three-quarter view, the rider banking toward the viewer but fully contained in the center safe area.
storm_wind_rider.background: Warm muted clay rooftops and amber-lit chimneys at dusk, motion-softened so the bright cool elemental remains the single readable subject.
storm_wind_rider.notes: Scraped from the draft brief this card was generated from (storm_wind_rider).

storm_zael_of_the_struck_sky.subject: Zael is a towering humanoid storm elemental formed from charcoal thundercloud, wind-torn silver rain sheets, and a hard cyan-white core. A jagged sky-fire wound splits the chest vertically as if the heavens struck him and never stopped burning. His two long arms sweep in opposing directions, each ending in a separate gold-white lightning arc, producing a clear double-strike silhouette rather than a tangled explosion. A stern face emerges from the cloud mass beneath a broken halo of two thin thunder-rings. His lower body tapers into a powerful spiral of wind above the ground. One figure only; no wings, no weapon, no ornate armor, no letters or rune-shaped lightning.
storm_zael_of_the_struck_sky.perspective: Low-angle three-quarter view of an airborne figure twisting into a twin-armed strike; the face, split chest-light, and paired lightning arcs stay within the central 70%.
storm_zael_of_the_struck_sky.background: A muted ochre ash plain with toppled pale stone under a dull overcast horizon, almost entirely desaturated and grounded; the saturated cyan and gold-white storm body dominates by hue and brightness.
storm_zael_of_the_struck_sky.notes: Scraped from the draft brief this card was generated from (storm_zael_of_the_struck_sky).

tide_venomfin.subject: A small amphibious reef beast with a low teal body, a broad crescent dorsal fin, translucent seafoam webbing, pale moon-silver spines, and two cold blue eyes. It rises halfway from a shallow pool, exposing one bead of luminous turquoise venom at the tip of a delicate hollow fin-spine; its slick scales and compact profile feel patient and dangerous rather than monstrous.
tide_venomfin.perspective: Water-level close three-quarter portrait with the entire creature and crescent fin centered, generous margin around the silhouette, and the single venom bead readable at thumbnail size.
tide_venomfin.background: A warm dim tide grotto lit by amber candles and distant ember-glow reflected across wet ochre rock, contrasting with the cool teal beast and pale mist.
tide_venomfin.notes: Venom is represented only by the one luminous bead and hollow spine. Keep the beast no larger than a house cat, with no giant teeth, attack splash, toxic cloud, extra animals, or catastrophic wave.

verdant_venomthorn.subject: A squat badger-sized plant beast built from knotted living roots, cedar-brown bark plates, and a dense crown of golden-honey thorn quills. It braces sideways across a narrow path with all four root-paws planted, while one dark emerald drop of venom hangs from the longest forward thorn. Fresh green shoots curl between the bark plates, making it feel stubbornly alive and defensive.
verdant_venomthorn.perspective: Low frontal three-quarter view at the creature's eye level, with its complete broad silhouette and thorn crown centered and every planted paw visible.
verdant_venomthorn.background: A pale blue-grey twilight clearing among cool weathered stones and thin silver mist, muted and spacious so the warm bark, green growth, and honey-gold thorns remain distinct.
verdant_venomthorn.notes: Bulwark reads through the path-blocking stance; Venom reads through one restrained drop. Keep it badger-sized, passive and sturdy rather than attacking, with no giant tree scale, toxic cloud, extra beasts, or explosive growth.

verdant_windroot_sprinter.subject: A small, wiry beast built like a greyhound crossed with a fern — legs of braided root, a body of quick fibrous grass, no bigger than a large dog. Low to the ground, mid-stride, ears back, moving fast and low rather than rearing up.
verdant_windroot_sprinter.perspective: Low, ground-level, side-on — emphasize speed and horizontal motion, not height.
verdant_windroot_sprinter.background: An open stretch of pale blue-grey dawn mist over chalky ground, cool and understated, with no dense green foliage behind the beast. The spare, high-key setting cleanly separates the warm russet-root and fern-gold body.
verdant_windroot_sprinter.notes: Palette priority: pale blue-grey and chalk background; warm russet, fern-gold, and muted olive subject; a faint honey-gold healing glow trails from its footfalls. Restore 2 Health to your hero on play, so the glow stays small and easy to miss, not a spectacle.

ward_boulderhide.subject: A squat four-legged stone guardian shaped like a stubborn pack animal, built from overlapping rounded granite plates that form a natural armored hide. Its small head is tucked safely behind high shoulder boulders; two pale quartz eyes glow beneath the brow. Rusted bronze bands brace the joints and sparse moss settles in sheltered seams. It plants itself sideways across a damaged doorway as a living bulwark. Make it sturdy and defensive rather than aggressive, compact rather than massive, with no weapon and no humanoid armor.
ward_boulderhide.perspective: Eye-level three-quarter view, centered on a low broad silhouette with all four planted feet visible.
ward_boulderhide.background: A narrow ruined gate passage warmed by amber lanterns and dusty dusk light, soft enough to separate the cool grey construct.
ward_boulderhide.notes: Scraped from the draft brief this card was generated from (stone_boulderhide).

ward_duras_the_ironmount.subject: Duras is a colossal living fortress-construct built from interlocked iron-grey granite slabs, with a mountain-like torso, battlement-shaped shoulders, and thick rusted-bronze braces holding the stone together. Pale quartz veins form a restrained inner glow across the chest and under a severe cliff-brow; sparse moss gathers only in protected cracks. Both immense fists are planted on the broken causeway as his arched forearms form a sheltering gate around the viewer, visually granting protection without showing other characters. His anatomy should feel architectural and original rather than like a human enlarged in stone. One clear subject, calm and unyielding; no handheld weapon, no castle on his back, no writing or carved runes.
ward_duras_the_ironmount.perspective: Heroic ground-level frontal view with a slight upward tilt, emphasizing a mountain-wide shoulder line and two planted fists while keeping the face and chest centered.
ward_duras_the_ironmount.background: A shattered fortress causeway under a luminous ember-red dawn, with warm dusty orange atmosphere and tiny distant masonry; the cool iron-grey colossus reads as one dark, immovable mass against the bright horizon.
ward_duras_the_ironmount.notes: Scraped from the draft brief this card was generated from (stone_duras_the_ironmount).

ward_earth_barrier.subject: A waist-high crescent of interlocking granite slabs pushes up through cracked cobbles in one tight protective arc. Pale quartz veins join the slabs like natural mortar, and a few mossy roots cinch them together. The barrier itself is the sole focal subject; behind it, only the indistinct lower silhouette of one protected traveler may be implied through dust, never becoming a competing figure. Show fresh earth at the base and a restrained halo of pale stone-light.
ward_earth_barrier.perspective: Close low-angle view of a compact crescent wall rising in the center, with its protective curve clearly readable.
ward_earth_barrier.background: A warm ember-lit alley of scorched plaster and dark timber, pushed into soft focus behind the cool pale barrier.
ward_earth_barrier.notes: No fortress wall, no enormous magical dome, and no violent eruption. Scraped from the draft brief this card was generated from (stone_earth_barrier).

ward_granite_guardian.subject: A sturdy Stonewarden construct stands squarely in one gatehouse doorway, about one-and-a-half times human height—broad enough to block the entrance, but nowhere near a colossus. Its body is assembled from practical granite slabs with iron-black joints, two rusted bronze shoulder clamps, narrow pale-quartz eyes, and small patches of moss in old seams. Both thick forearms are held across the opening in a simple defensive posture, with no separate shield or weapon. Its feet remain fully visible and firmly planted on ordinary flagstones. Calm, durable, and workmanlike rather than legendary.
ward_granite_guardian.perspective: Straight eye-level view from several paces away, showing the complete doorway-sized guardian and clear planted stance without a heroic low-angle exaggeration.
ward_granite_guardian.background: A modest rebuilt gatehouse lit by warm amber lanterns at dusk, with simple ochre plaster and timber behind the cool grey construct.
ward_granite_guardian.notes: No battlement shoulders, mountain anatomy, glowing chest core, raised fortress wall, debris explosion, tiny people for scale, or dramatic skyline. Scraped from the draft brief this card was generated from (stone_granite_guardian).

ward_pebble_sentinel.subject: A knee-high defensive construct assembled from five rounded granite fieldstones, with two broad pebble arms locked together like a tiny barricade. A narrow rusted-bronze band holds its torso stones in place, pale quartz eyes glow beneath a slab-like brow, and small patches of moss soften the joints. It plants its short feet stubbornly between two fallen wall blocks, protective and immovable despite its humble size.
ward_pebble_sentinel.perspective: Low close three-quarter view at the construct's eye level, with its complete compact silhouette centered and obvious scale cues from loose masonry and a discarded iron nail nearby.
ward_pebble_sentinel.background: A ruined watch-post doorway lit by warm amber lantern light and sparse drifting embers, with dark timber and softly blurred ochre stone behind the cool granite subject.
ward_pebble_sentinel.notes: Bulwark reads through the locked-arm stance and planted feet. Keep it knee-high, endearing but not cute, with no giant proportions, attack pose, weapon, or explosive magic.

ward_rock_golem.subject: A workmanlike humanoid golem assembled from angular quarry blocks, roughly twice a person's width but only modestly taller than a doorway. It braces in a patient guarding stance with broad forearms held together like a shield. Its face is a simple iron-black inset plate with two pale quartz eyes; rusted bronze clamps hold the shoulders and knees, and thin moss marks its age. Keep the design plain, practical, and visibly less imposing than a granite guardian or siege golem.
ward_rock_golem.perspective: Slight low-angle full-body portrait, centered, with both feet and the complete head safely inside the central frame area.
ward_rock_golem.background: A warm dim quarry workshop at dusk with amber braziers, weathered timber braces, and muted clay walls.
ward_rock_golem.notes: No weapon, no ornate armor, no colossal scale, and no roaring pose. Scraped from the draft brief this card was generated from (stone_rock_golem).

ward_siege_golem.subject: A purpose-built Stonewarden siege golem advances through a shattered gate: squat, broad, and brutally functional, made from interlocking granite blocks bound by iron-black pivots and rusted bronze hoops. One shoulder and forearm fuse into a massive wedge-shaped breaching shield, while the opposite hand presses into the earth and sends a pale quartz reinforcement pulse through its own cracked armor. Its low head is tucked safely behind the shield, with two small quartz eyes under a slab brow. Unlike Duras, it is a finite battlefield engine rather than a living fortress—heavy enough to hold a breach, compact enough to fit through one. Sparse moss in old seams, no rider, no handheld weapon, no wheels, no castle on its back, no carved writing or runes.
ward_siege_golem.perspective: Low three-quarter view from just outside a breached gate, showing its wedge-shaped shield shoulder and planted stance as one broad silhouette.
ward_siege_golem.background: A warm smoke-filled fortress breach under amber-orange afternoon light, with distant burning dust and softened brickwork; the cool granite golem remains the dark foreground mass.
ward_siege_golem.notes: Scraped from the draft brief this card was generated from (stone_siege_golem).

ward_stone_throw.subject: A compact volley of five fist-sized granite stones skips outward in one low, fan-shaped sweep across the courtyard, launched by a barely visible shove of earth from a cracked paving stone. Make the leading stone the clear focal subject, with pale quartz chips and thin moss seams catching the light. The action suggests a modest defensive spell striking several nearby foes without showing any enemies. Keep the effect physical and weighty: dust puffs, two short impact chips, no explosion, no giant boulder, no caster, and no battlefield-wide destruction.

ward_stone_throw.background: A warm, dim amber-lit ruin courtyard with charred timber and muted ember glow, kept soft and subordinate behind the cool granite projectiles.

neutral_spellwarden.subject: A weathered settlement scholar in a stone-grey coat raises a round aged-bronze warding plate as three small arcane sparks spiral into a restrained amber knot above its blank center. neutral_ironclad_bulwark.subject: A squat ironclad settlement construct braces behind two overlapping riveted shield plates, its body built from iron-black boiler sections, aged-bronze hinges, and a single warm lantern-amber core. neutral_venomscale_drake.subject: A lean hound-sized drake crouches along a broken aqueduct, its overlapping slate-grey scales edged in moss green and its throat pouch glowing a restrained toxic lime. One clear venom bead gathers at a short ivory fang while, below the parapet, one tiny ochre-clad aqueduct worker drops a pale bucket and scrambles away from the creature.

neutral_venomscale_drake.background: A warm dusty coral sunset over pale ruined arches, opposing the cool slate body and toxic-green throat.

neutral_duneborn_construct.subject: A broad four-legged construct rises from wind-packed sand, built around a dark iron frame clad in sun-bleached sandstone plates and held by aged-bronze straps. Its wedge-shaped front slab lowers into a defensive brace while a small amber furnace-eye glows beneath the overhang.

neutral_searing_quill.subject: A single long bronze-and-ivory writing quill lies diagonally above a dark stone tablet, its feather burned to ember-red filaments and its sharpened metal nib glowing molten orange. One curling line of heat scorches the tablet surface without forming any letter or symbol.

ember_cinderplate_golem.subject: A compact Emberward golem lunges from one planted foot, its body assembled from overlapping char-black furnace plates with molten-orange seams and a blunt ember-red shoulder ram. One gold spark sprays from a cracked elbow as the forward fist drives through a low barricade, while one tiny pale-clad yard watchman recoils behind the far edge to make the golem's dangerous speed feel immediate.
ember_cinderplate_golem.perspective: Low dynamic three-quarter action view with the entire golem, forward fist, and planted rear foot contained within the central frame.
ember_cinderplate_golem.background: A pale cold-grey ash yard under blue smoke, opposing the dark armor and molten seams while leaving the silhouette clean.
ember_cinderplate_golem.notes: The 6/3 profile reads as high force and brittle construction. Keep the lone watchman tiny and subordinate. No giant scale, defensive shield, weapon, volcano, humanoid face, or explosion filling the frame.

ember_magmacore_warden.subject: A massive but doorway-scale elemental warden plants both fists like buttresses, its char-black basalt torso enclosing one deep molten-orange magma core behind thick gold-riveted ribs. Ember-red heat vents rise from the shoulders while broad cracked-rock forearms form a protective arch.
ember_magmacore_warden.perspective: Low frontal three-quarter portrait with the full warden, both bracing fists, and bright central core centered and safely inside the frame.
ember_magmacore_warden.background: A pale blue-grey mountain pass veiled in cold steam, creating strong temperature contrast with the molten core and dark volcanic body.
ember_magmacore_warden.notes: Bulwark is a stable arched stance, not a shield spell. No lava giant scale, erupting volcano, weapon, roaring mouth, wings, or uncontrolled inferno.

ember_heat_surge.subject: A single compressed wave of transparent heat rolls forward across cracked black forge tiles, bending the air into a clear lens and lifting a narrow crest of molten-orange sparks. The foremost tile flashes ember red along its fracture just before the wave passes.
ember_heat_surge.perspective: Very low ground-level side view with the heat lens, spark crest, and glowing cracked tile forming one centered horizontal action.
ember_heat_surge.background: A cool desaturated steel-blue foundry corridor fading into pale smoke, so the warm distortion and sparks remain the sole focal energy.
ember_heat_surge.notes: Show heat through refraction and a restrained spark crest, not a fireball, explosion, lava flood, caster, enemy, or text-like pattern.

verdant_ironbark_elder.subject: An ancient treefolk warden, roughly two men tall, whose cedar-brown heartwood is armoured in overlapping plates of iron-hard bark, weathered grey at the edges and seamed with golden-honey sap where the plates meet. It stands squarely with both arms folded across its chest like a closed gate, moss and small ferns growing in the crooks of its shoulders, its face a deep knot of grain with two slow amber lights for eyes. Roots have grown down over its feet and into the ground, as if it has stood in this one spot long enough to become part of it.
verdant_ironbark_elder.perspective: Slight low frontal three-quarter view from near ground level, the whole braced silhouette centred and both planted feet visible — one figure, framed as a figure, not as a landscape.
verdant_ironbark_elder.background: A pale blue-grey overcast sky over a bare chalk ridge — cool, flat and nearly empty — so the warm cedar-brown body, honey sap seams and weathered grey plates separate cleanly from it.
verdant_ironbark_elder.notes: Bulwark reads through the folded-arms, gate-like stance and the rooted feet, never through a literal wall or a shield. Keep it to a single figure at mid-board scale: no forest, no titanic world-tree, no glowing magic, no second creature.

verdant_elderroot_colossus.subject: A hulking four-limbed shape woven entirely out of thick living roots and packed dark earth, with no face — just a dense knot where a head would be, and a chest cavity glowing faint honey-gold from the sap inside it. It is walking forward with real weight behind it, one root-fist already through a low drystone wall that is coming apart ahead of it, clods and small stones spraying out at knee height.
verdant_elderroot_colossus.perspective: Frontal three-quarter view at chest height, the whole striding silhouette centred, the breaking wall kept low in the frame so nothing competes with the body.
verdant_elderroot_colossus.background: A cold pale-grey dusk over open chalk downland, muted and thinly lit, so the warm root-brown mass and the honey-gold chest light read instantly.
verdant_elderroot_colossus.notes: Overwhelm reads through the wall breaking, not through scale. Hold it to roughly two men tall — this is a 4-mana card and must NOT be staged as a titan, a mountain-sized giant, or a landscape-wide catastrophe. No face, no glowing eyes, no other figures.

verdant_menders_bloom.subject: One large flower opening in close-up, its petals layered cedar-brown at the base and warm honey-gold at the tips, with a soft green light welling out of its centre like a held breath. Fine green threads of new growth reach down from the bloom and lace closed across a split in the dark bark beneath it, drawing the wound shut — the mending is caught mid-knit, in progress, not finished.
verdant_menders_bloom.perspective: Tight, intimate close-up at the flower's own level, the bloom and the closing seam centred together — small in scale and quiet, never a spell cast over a battlefield.
verdant_menders_bloom.background: Cool blue-grey shadow and wet dark stone falling away sharply behind the bloom, deep in value and almost colourless, so the warm gold petals and green light glow out of it.
verdant_menders_bloom.notes: The spell restores health to one ally, so this is a single contained act of mending: no radiant burst, no beams, no healing wave washing over a field, no runes or spell circles. No hands, no caster, no creature — the bloom and the wound it is closing are the whole image.

verdant_thalens_ancient.subject: A towering ancient of the deep wood — a walking tree with a trunk-body of fissured cedar bark, a crown of antlered branches still in full leaf, and a long slow stride. Golden honey sap runs bright in the fissures of its chest and down its forelimbs like veins beneath the bark. One heavy limb sweeps forward and low, shearing the top off a ruined stone wall as it comes on, leaves and bark-dust trailing behind it. A mantle of living canopy hangs from its shoulders, echoing Thalen Greenmantle's own cloak without depicting him.
verdant_thalens_ancient.perspective: Low heroic three-quarter view looking up at it, the full antlered crown inside the frame and uncropped, the ruined wall small at its feet to carry the scale.
verdant_thalens_ancient.background: A cold pale-quartz mountain face under a thin, near-white sky — high in value and drained of colour — so the deep green canopy and sap-gold trunk read as one dark silhouette against it.
verdant_thalens_ancient.notes: This is the Verdant legendary and should be the most commanding shape in the class: Bulwark through the immovable rooted trailing leg, Overwhelm through the wall shearing away. One creature only — do not paint Thalen Greenmantle himself, and do not fill the frame with forest.

verdant_worldroot_behemoth.subject: A four-legged behemoth about the size of a war elephant, its whole body a knotted mass of pale enormous roots torn up from far underground, dark wet earth still packed between them and shedding as it moves. Its head is low and blunt with no eyes, ringed by a collar of broken root-tips like tusks. It is mid-charge, shouldering straight through the trunk of a dead tree that splinters across its chest, hind legs still dragging fresh soil up out of the ground behind it.
verdant_worldroot_behemoth.perspective: Side-on three-quarter charging view at head height, the full body length inside the frame with the splintering trunk crossing low, so the motion reads left-to-right at a glance.
verdant_worldroot_behemoth.background: Cold pale blue-grey rainfall over flat drowned ground, low in contrast and desaturated, so the warm root-brown bulk and the dark packed earth are the only solid mass in the frame.
verdant_worldroot_behemoth.notes: Overwhelm reads through the splintering trunk and the earth being hauled up. It is a beast, not a treefolk — no face, no arms, no antlers, nothing humanoid, no rider. Big, but one charging animal rather than a landscape event.

verdant_canopy_seer.subject: A tall, long-limbed figure perched high in a fork of branches, wrapped in a hooded mantle of layered green leaves that hangs down over the wood beneath it. Its face is bark-grained and calm with the eyes closed, one hand pressed flat to the branch it is reading; just above that hand a single seed hangs in the air, split open, a thin thread of honey-gold light unwinding out of it. Long-limbed and unarmoured rather than bulky — a watcher, not a fighter, but full-grown and a real presence at its own scale.
verdant_canopy_seer.perspective: Level three-quarter view from just outside the branch fork, at the seer's own height, the seated figure and the floating seed centred together.
verdant_canopy_seer.background: A cold pale-grey dawn haze filling the space beyond the branches, flat and near-white, silhouetting the green mantle and cedar limbs with no second layer of foliage behind them.
verdant_canopy_seer.notes: Drawing a card reads as the split seed and its one thread of light — keep it small and quiet. No glowing eyes, no visionary imagery, no runes, no floating cards, and no forest depth behind the branch; the emptiness is what makes the silhouette read at board size.

ward_earthwardens_maul.subject: A short, brutally heavy warhammer shown whole: a squared block of granite bound in rusted bronze bands for a head, on a full-length iron-black haft running down to a banded butt cap, the haft roughly two and a half times the height of the head so the thing reads as a weapon a warden actually swings. The striking face is chipped and pale where it has been used, moss has taken hold in the seams of the bronze and in the pitting along one flat, and a vein of pale quartz runs through the stone and catches the light.
ward_earthwardens_maul.perspective: Set WELL BACK and shot with a long lens — near-orthographic, minimal perspective falloff, the maul presented close to its true side profile with NO foreshortening. The ENTIRE weapon is in frame, head AND full-length haft down to its butt cap, standing roughly upright and filling most of the circle's height. Nothing is cropped and nothing is truncated.
ward_earthwardens_maul.background: A dim, warm amber field — low ember-glow in hazy dark air, no setting and no ground — opposing the cold granite grey, iron-black and moss-green of the weapon itself.
ward_earthwardens_maul.notes: Weapon art renders into a CIRCULAR SOCKET, so keep everything inside the middle 60%. The previous pass showed a fine granite head sitting on a haft that stopped dead about a hand's width below it, which reads as a broken or miniature weapon. A maul is short enough to picture WHOLE, so picture it whole: pull the camera back until the full haft and its butt cap fit, rather than cutting the handle off. The head should still be the dominant mass. It grants Bulwark, so it should look like something that plants and holds rather than something that swings fast. The object alone — no hand, no wielder, no ground, no scene, no figure of any kind.

ember_scorch_blade.subject: A broad, heavy single-edged cleaver-sword. The blade is dark char-black steel split by a wide molten fissure running its whole length, orange-white at the core, throwing loose gold sparks off the cutting edge. The crossguard is a short bar of blackened iron and the grip is bound in scorched leather. Heat visibly distorts the air along the spine of the blade.
ember_scorch_blade.perspective: Set well back and shot with a long lens — near-orthographic, minimal perspective falloff, the sword presented close to its true side profile with no foreshortening. The ENTIRE weapon is in frame, point to pommel, held at a shallow angle off vertical and filling most of the circle's height rather than crossing corner to corner. Nothing is cropped.
ember_scorch_blade.background: A cold, dim blue-black night field with faint slate-grey haze, no setting and no ground, opposing the molten orange and gold of the blade.
ember_scorch_blade.notes: Weapon art renders into a CIRCULAR SOCKET on the hero frame — keep everything inside the middle 60%, compose COMPACT, and never lay the blade corner to corner. This must NOT resemble Cinder Lance (ember_cinder_lance), which today ships the byte-identical file: that one is a slim, mostly-dark thrusting lance head with only thin ember cracks; this is a BROAD cleaver blade that is actively molten and throwing sparks. The object alone — no hand, no wielder, no ground, no scene.
